chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The morning (Fajr) is that which, when you see it spreading horizontally, it is as if it is the white light of Sura.

key_terms.الصبح: Subh/Fajr — the dawn, specifically the true dawn (al-fajr al-sadiq) that marks the beginning of the Fajr prayer time
key_terms.بياض سورى: Whiteness of Sura — a comparison to the distinct white appearance of the ancient city of Sura, a well-known landmark in Iraq used as a reference by the Imam
key_terms.معترضاً: Spreading horizontally/across — describing the horizontal spread of the true dawn light on the horizon

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Sadiq define the true dawn (Fajr) for the prayer time?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the true onset of the Fajr (dawn) prayer time by a visual description: the true dawn appears as a horizontal white light spread across the horizon, likened to the white gleam of the city of Sura in Iraq. This distinguishes the 'true dawn' (al-fajr al-sadiq) from the 'false dawn' (al-fajr al-kadhib), which appears as a vertical column of light. This legal ruling was given to disciples of the Imam to precisely determine the time for the obligatory Fajr prayer, the end of the night prayer, and the end of the permissible eating period during Ramadan.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Atiyya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The morning, it is which, when you see it horizontally, it is as if it is a white edge’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Ali ibn ‘ Atiyyah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Dawn is when you find a white line like the whiteness of Sur 5 (a certain section of Euphrates river in Iraq) 5 ”
